subject: Revisiting commit tiers + per-token threshold structure for renewal
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir@acme-health.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example, karthik_iyer@redwood.example
Cc: Olivia Price <olivia.price@procure-acme.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API commit question & threshold structure

Marissa / Karthik —

Thanks again for the renewal materials. We're running a tighter forecast for H2 and need to revisit the committed tokens for the Hosted API. A few asks from procurement and engineering: 

- Can we create a smaller base commit (we're looking at ~700k tokens/month over a 12-month term) but keep a steeper discount curve as we hit higher cumulative usage?
- Can Redwood put an uplift cap on renewal pricing so we don't see more than a 15% year-over-year list increase?
- We need a simple true-up model (quarterly) and an option to burst above commit without punitive overage pricing — ideally a per-token overage that steps down once we pass certain monthly thresholds.

Attached a short forecast and the SOW procurement asked for. Open to a quick call to walk numbers.

Samir
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme HealthTech

Attachments: Acme_HighLevel_forecast_Q4.pdf (pdf, 120KB), Procurement_SOW_v2.docx (docx, 64KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.example <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Samir Khan <samir@acme-health.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example, lauren_bishop@redwood.example
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit question & threshold structure

Samir —

Appreciate the clarity and the forecast — this is helpful. Quick responses and a proposed framework below: 

- Flexed base commit: we can offer a 12-month term with a 700k tokens/month committed baseline.
- Tiered per-token pricing (example):
  - 0–700k (committed): $0.0026 / token
  - 700k–2.5M: $0.0020 / token
  - 2.5M–10M: $0.0016 / token
  - >10M: $0.0013 / token

- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with credit applied to the following quarter.
- Overages: pay-as-you-go overage at $0.0030 / token with automatic step-down once monthly usage stays above the next threshold for two consecutive months.
- Renewal uplift cap: we can contractually cap list pricing increases to 15% YoY for the first renewal year (legal will need to confirm).

Karthik — tagging you for comments on committing flexibility and any finance constraints. Lauren — I'd like a quick read from enterprise before we send a formal proposal to procurement.

Can we lock a 30-minute slot Friday to run the numbers?

—Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.example
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit question & threshold structure

Thanks — I like Marissa's structure but a couple of adjustments from a finance/ops POV: 

- Make the step-down thresholds cumulative over the contract year rather than strictly monthly to avoid month-to-month volatility (e.g., annualized usage bands for price breaks).
- Offer a soft-commit option: 50% firm commit / 50% flexible commit. Flexible portion is billed at a slightly higher rate but qualifies for true-up credits if annualized usage meets thresholds.
- For overage protection, propose a temporary burst buffer (up to 20% above committed baseline) billed at an agreed intermediate rate instead of immediate overage pricing.

Ben — can you confirm whether legal will accept a 15% uplift cap for the first renewal year and if finance needs any minimums for the soft-commit structure?

Karthik
Head of Revenue Operations

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API commit question & threshold structure

Team / Samir —

Legal reviewed the uplift cap ask; we can accept a 15% cap on list increases for the first renewal year but need to include language that excludes changes tied to material changes in underlying cloud/infra costs or taxes/regulatory fees. Finance is okay with the soft-commit construct provided the contract includes an annual minimum of $150k ARR.

Also, procurement asked for a DocuSign-ready SOW and clear billing contact. I've uploaded a draft SOW into the HubSpot deal and added a DocuSign packet link below. If Acme is good with the numbers, I can spin a formal quote with those terms.

Ben Carter
Senior Commercial Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

Related links: https://docusign.example.com/packet/ABCD-1234

Samir —

Thanks — sounds like we're converging. Next steps: 

1) Ben will prepare a DocuSign-ready SOW and quote with:
   - 12-month term
   - 700k tokens/month committed baseline
   - soft-commit 50/50 option and annual minimum $150k ARR
   - tiered pricing and quarterly true-ups as outlined
   - renewal uplift cap 15% YoY (exclusions for cloud/infrastructure/tax pass-throughs)
2) We'll attach the forecast and SOW to the HubSpot deal and send to procurement (Olivia) for signature.
3) Schedule: Ben to share DocuSign packet by EOD Thursday; target signature week of Sep 20.

Can we confirm a 30-minute call Friday at 10:00 AM PT to finalize numbers? If that works, I'll send an invite.

—Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
